_note: SPECIFIC-question equivalence set. Anchors = verbatim NIST SP 800-171r2 requirement statements (real, specific, multi-clause). Positives = AUTHORED lexically-varied meaning-preserving paraphrases (flagged). Hard negatives = different real requirements from the same control family (natural).

questions.text: How should an organization monitor, control, and protect communications at the external boundaries and key internal boundaries of organizational systems?
How should an organization implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are physically or logically separated from internal networks?
How should an organization deny network communications traffic by default and allow network communications traffic by exception (deny all, permit by exception)?
How should an organization implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of CUI during transmission unless otherwise protected by alternative physical safeguards?
How should an organization employ FIPS-validated cryptography when used to protect the confidentiality of CUI?
How should an organization protect the confidentiality of CUI at rest?
How should an organization terminate network connections associated with communications sessions at the end of the sessions or after a defined period of inactivity?
How should an organization prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and provide indication of devices in use to users present at the device?
How should an organization authenticate or verify the identities of users, processes, or devices as a prerequisite to allowing access to organizational systems?
How should an organization use multifactor authentication for local and network access to privileged accounts and for network access to non-privileged accounts?
How should an organization enforce a minimum password complexity and change of characters when new passwords are created?
How should an organization prohibit password reuse for a specified number of generations?
How should an organization store and transmit only cryptographically-protected passwords?
How should an organization disable identifiers after a defined period of inactivity?
How should an organization limit system access to authorized users, processes acting on behalf of authorized users, and devices including other systems?
How should an organization limit system access to the types of transactions and functions that authorized users are permitted to execute?
How should an organization control the flow of CUI in accordance with approved authorizations?
How should an organization employ the principle of least privilege, including for specific security functions and privileged accounts?
How should an organization monitor and control remote access sessions?
How should an organization employ cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality of remote access sessions?
How should an organization verify and control or limit connections to and use of external systems?
How should an organization control CUI posted or processed on publicly accessible systems?

How should an organization establish and maintain baseline configurations and inventories of organizational systems including hardware, software, firmware, and documentation throughout the system development life cycle?
How should an organization establish and enforce security configuration settings for information technology products employed in organizational systems?
How should an organization employ the principle of least functionality by configuring organizational systems to provide only essential capabilities?
How should an organization restrict, disable, or prevent the use of nonessential programs, functions, ports, protocols, and services?

How should an organization apply deny-by-exception (blacklisting) policy to prevent the use of unauthorized software or deny-all, permit-by-exception (whitelisting) policy to allow the use of authorized software?
How should an organization control and monitor user-installed software?
How should an organization identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner?
How should an organization provide protection from malicious code at designated locations within organizational systems?
How should an organization update malicious code protection mechanisms when new releases are available?
How should an organization monitor organizational systems, including inbound and outbound communications traffic, to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks?
How should a company observe, govern, and safeguard the data flowing across both its outer network perimeter and its important interior network divisions?
How should an org place internet-facing services onto separate network segments that are kept physically or logically apart from its internal LAN?
How should a firewall be set so that every packet is dropped unless a specific rule explicitly permits it (a default-deny stance)?
How should an organization use encryption so that CUI cannot be read while in transit, unless equivalent physical protection is already in place?
How should a contractor ensure any cryptography that safeguards CUI confidentiality is validated under FIPS?
How should an organization keep stored CUI confidential while it sits at rest?
How should identities of people, service processes, and hardware be verified before they are granted access to company systems?
How should an org require two or more authentication factors for on-site and remote sign-ins to admin accounts, and for remote sign-ins to regular user accounts?
How should newly created passwords be forced to meet a minimum complexity bar and to change enough characters from the prior one?
How should the system stop users from reusing any of their last several passwords?
How should passwords be handled so that only cryptographically protected forms are ever stored or sent over the wire?
How should access to systems be restricted to only approved people, the processes running on their behalf, and authorized equipment including other systems?
How should each authorized user be confined to only the specific transaction types and functions they are permitted to run?
How should the movement of CUI through the environment be governed strictly according to the approvals that authorize it?
How should the org grant each account only the minimum privileges it needs, including for security-relevant functions and administrator accounts?
How should remote-access sessions be watched and kept under control by the organization?
How should encryption be applied to keep the contents of remote-access sessions confidential?
How should connections to, and the use of, systems outside the organization's control be vetted and either governed or capped?
How should an org create and keep current a baseline build and asset inventory (hardware, software, firmware, docs) across the whole system life cycle?
How should hardened security configuration settings be defined and enforced for the IT products used in company systems?
How should systems be pared down so they expose only the capabilities that are actually essential (least functionality)?
How should nonessential programs, functions, network ports, protocols, and services be locked down, turned off, or blocked?
How should software execution be governed either by blocklisting unauthorized programs or by allowlisting only approved ones?
How should software and system defects be found, reported, and remediated promptly?
How should defenses against malware be placed at the chosen points inside the organization's systems?
How should the organization watch its systems and the traffic entering and leaving them to spot attacks and signs of impending attacks?
How should information marked CUI that is published or handled on public-facing systems be kept under control?
How should communication sessions have their network connections closed out when the session ends or after a set idle period?
